# package eth

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport/eth"
```

Package eth is the Ethernet transport of OPC UA PubSub (Part 14 §7.3.3, transport profile pubsub-eth-uadp): UADP NetworkMessages as the payload of Ethernet II frames with EtherType 0xB62C, without IP and UDP headers.

Importing the package registers the "opc.eth" scheme with [transport.Register](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport#Register).

#### Addresses {#hdr-Addresses}

The URL of a connection is opc.eth://\<host>\[:\<VID>\[.\<PCP>]] (see [ParseURL](#func-parseurl)): host is the destination MAC address, unicast, multicast (opc.eth://01-00-5e-00-00-01) or broadcast; with a VID the frames carry an IEEE 802.1Q tag with that VLAN identifier and priority code point.

Config.Interface (NetworkInterface of NetworkAddressDataType) names the interface ("eth0") and is required; the frames are sent with its MAC address as source.

A subscription receives the frames of EtherType 0xB62C that arrive on the interface and are addressed to its MAC address, to the broadcast address or, if the URL is a multicast address, to that group, which it joins. The VLAN tag of a received frame is not a filter: on Linux the kernel removes the tag before raw sockets see the frame. To receive one VLAN only, use the VLAN interface (eth0.100) and a URL without VID. Frames this host sends are received too unless Config.MulticastLoopback is false.

#### Size {#hdr-Size}

A NetworkMessage is at most MaxPayload (1500) bytes, or the MTU of the interface if that is smaller (on the BSDs minus the 4 bytes of a VLAN tag); Send rejects larger ones with [transport.ErrMessageTooLarge](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport#ErrMessageTooLarge). Short frames are padded to the Ethernet minimum (60 bytes) by the hardware: a receiver gets the padding after a small NetworkMessage.

#### Operating systems {#hdr-Operating_systems}

Linux uses AF\_PACKET raw sockets (CAP\_NET\_RAW or root), macOS and FreeBSD use BPF devices (/dev/bpf\*, root or read-write access to the devices; joining a multicast group needs root on macOS). macOS hides the MAC address of an interface from processes without privileges: the kernel still sets the right source address, but a subscription then accepts every unicast frame the interface delivers. On other systems Open returns ErrNotSupported.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// EtherType is the IANA-registered EtherType of OPC UA UADP
	// NetworkMessages (Part 14 §7.3.3).
	EtherType = 0xB62C
	// tpid8021Q is the EtherType of an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag.

	// tpid8021AD is the EtherType of an IEEE 802.1ad (QinQ) service tag.

	// MaxPayload is the largest NetworkMessage of a frame: Part 14 §7.3.3
	// limits frames to 1522 bytes, "MaxNetworkMessageSize is typically
	// 1500" once the 22 bytes of addresses, EtherType, VLAN tag and frame
	// check sequence are subtracted. The tag does not reduce it: a tagged
	// frame may be 4 bytes longer than an untagged one.
	MaxPayload = 1500
)
```

Frame layout (Part 14 §7.3.3, Table 200; IEEE 802.3 Ethernet II with an optional IEEE 802.1Q tag):

	destination MAC   6 bytes
	source MAC        6 bytes
	[TPID 0x8100      2 bytes   802.1Q tag, optional
	 TCI              2 bytes   PCP (3 bits) | DEI (1 bit) | VID (12 bits)]
	EtherType 0xB62C  2 bytes
	NetworkMessage    up to 1500 bytes

The frame check sequence is added and removed by the hardware.

```go
const MaxVID = 4094
```

MaxVID is the largest VLAN identifier: 4095 (0xFFF) is reserved (IEEE 802.1Q §9.6).

```go
const Scheme = "opc.eth"
```

Scheme is the URL scheme of the Ethernet transport.

```go
const (

	// the kernel allows 4 more bytes for a tagged frame
	// the receive tap marks the frames this host sends
	// Supported reports whether the OS has an implementation.
	Supported = true
)
```

```go
var ErrNotSupported = fmt.Errorf("pubsub/transport/eth: the Ethernet transport is not supported on this OS: %w", errors.ErrUnsupported)
```

ErrNotSupported is returned by Open on an OS without raw Ethernet access for this package (anything but Linux, macOS and FreeBSD).

## Types

### type Address

```go
type Address struct {
	// MAC is the destination (or, for a received message, the source)
	// MAC address; nil for an address without host (receive only).
	MAC net.HardwareAddr
	// VLAN reports whether the address has a VID: frames are sent with an
	// IEEE 802.1Q tag.
	VLAN bool
	// VID is the VLAN identifier, 0 to 4094. VID 0 is a priority tag: the
	// frame belongs to no VLAN and only carries the PCP.
	VID uint16
	// PCP is the priority code point of the tag, 0 to 7.
	PCP uint8
}
```

Address is the address of an Ethernet connection, the part of an opc.eth:// URL after the scheme (Part 14 §7.3.3):

	opc.eth://<host>[:<VID>[.<PCP>]]

It is also the [net.Addr](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Addr) of the sender of a received message.

#### func ParseURL

```go
func ParseURL(url string) (Address, error)
```

ParseURL parses an opc.eth:// URL (Part 14 §7.3.3):

	opc.eth://<host>[:<VID>[.<PCP>]]

host is a MAC address as six groups of hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens (01-23-45-67-89-ab), unicast, multicast or broadcast (ff-ff-ff-ff-ff-ff), or empty for a connection that only receives. The specification also allows a host name or IP address "if the system can resolve them to a MAC address"; resolving is not supported, such an address is an error. VID is the decimal VLAN identifier (0 to 4094), PCP the decimal priority code point (0 to 7). A path, query or fragment is ignored.

Conn is an Ethernet PubSub connection.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(ctx context.Context, cfg transport.Config) (*Conn, error)
```

Open opens an Ethernet connection for cfg.URL on cfg.Interface. It opens the sending link if the URL has a MAC address; the receiving link is opened by Subscribe.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close closes the links, leaves the multicast group and waits for the receive goroutine to end (unless it is called from a handler, which runs on that goroutine).

#### func (Conn) LocalAddr

```go
func (c *Conn) LocalAddr() net.Addr
```

LocalAddr returns the address of the interface: its MAC address and the VLAN tag of the URL.

#### func (Conn) MaxMessageSize

```go
func (c *Conn) MaxMessageSize() int
```

MaxMessageSize is the largest payload Send accepts.

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, payload []byte, _ transport.PublishOptions) error
```

Send transmits one NetworkMessage in one frame to the address of the connection. A NetworkMessage larger than MaxMessageSize fails with [transport.ErrMessageTooLarge](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport#ErrMessageTooLarge): the transport does not split messages.

#### func (Conn) Subscribe

```go
func (c *Conn) Subscribe(ctx context.Context, _ string, _ byte, h transport.Handler) (func() error, error)
```

Subscribe delivers every NetworkMessage received on the connection's interface and address to h. topic and qos are ignored. The first Subscribe opens the receiving link and joins the multicast group; an error doing so is returned here.
